thread:
alex: Heads-up — control-plane upgrade to 1.27 went through in us-west-2 last night. After the upgrade cluster-autoscaler stopped scaling GPU nodepools; a bunch of GPU jobs are Pending with nodeSelector nvidia.com/gpu.
rita: Can you paste CA logs and confirm the CA image tag?
alex: CA image we run: gcr.io/redwood/cluster-autoscaler:v1.26.4 (we hadn't bumped it yet). Logs show a panic while parsing nodegroup/nodepool objects.
alex: ```panic: interface conversion: map[string]interface {} is not string
goroutine 123 [running]:
  k8s.io/autoscaler/cluster-autoscaler/cloudprovider/aws.(*ASG).Refresh(...)
E0301 02:12:34.567890 1 scale_up.go:215] Failed to find any node groups for pod gpu-job-9
```
rita: Looks like the cloud provider NodePool API shape changed in the k8s control-plane upgrade — labels moved under spec.template.metadata.labels and CA's nodegroup parser expects them in a different place. CA can't match templates so GPU pools are effectively ignored.
evan: Short-term mitigation: manually scale GPU nodegroups up so pods land, and pin CA to v1.26 until we patch it. Example commands: `kubectl scale nodegroup gpu-ndp --replicas=5 -n kube-system` or use cloud console. For the helm CA: `helm upgrade --set image.tag=v1.26.4 cluster-autoscaler ./chart`
mike: We already did manual scaling for two pools, pods started scheduling. Cost spike observed: ~12 extra GPUs for a few hours. We need a rollback and a safer upgrade plan.
sasha: We should block future control-plane upgrades until CA / cloudprovider compatibility test is added to our upgrade gates. Also add an e2e that validates GPU pools scale after upgrade.
alex: Agreed. Immediate plan: 1) pin CA in affected clusters to v1.26, 2) add a small mutating patch as a hotfix to nodepool objects (copy/duplicate labels into the location CA expects), 3) upstream a vendor/adapter fix to CA, 4) schedule a maintenance window to re-upgrade after CA patch and run the new e2es. I'll produce a runbook.
deploy-bot: Deployment note: rollback scheduled for cluster 'us-west-2-prod' at 2024-03-01T06:00:00Z (automated rollback slot).
k8s-alerts: ALERT: 24 pending pods with GPU selectors in us-west-2 (avg wait 9m) — severity: P2.
rita: I'm adding a temporary kubectl patch we can apply to the nodepool CR to copy labels into `spec.template.metadata.labels` so CA can detect GPU label quickly: `kubectl patch nodepool gpu-ndp -p '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"labels":{"nvidia.com/gpu":"true"}}}}}'` — use only as hotfix and remove after CA update.
evan: If we do the mutation, make sure taints/tolerations remain consistent. I'll add a cleanup job to remove that patch post-fix.
mike: Cost hit estimate: ~12 GPUs * $2.40/hr * 3 hours = ~$86.4. Not huge but if this repeats it becomes meaningful. Add alert on CA failure/errors so we can detect earlier.
sasha: Filing postmortem and tagging Platform for SLA impact calc. Also adding note to stop other cluster upgrades until we've validated CA compatibility.
alex: Filed INF-1429 with initial notes and timeline: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-1429. I'll attach logs and the runbook.
evan: PR with upstream patch: https://github.com/redwood/cluster-autoscaler/pull/98 — small change to accept labels in both `metadata.labels` and `spec.template.metadata.labels`, plus unit tests.
mike: I'll own rollback playbook and cost reconciliation.
sasha: I'll own the postmortem and upgrade gating.
rita: :thumbsup: assigning tasks: evan -> CA PR, mike -> rollback & cost, sasha -> postmortem.
alex: Thanks all — I'll post the final runbook and close the loop once CA is pinned and the hotfix is applied.
